and a hundred thousand captives were sold,
and the rest were divided into servitude.
And this was an evil end for the Jews in Jerusalem.
Now concerning the great trial that took place in the city,
and the things that the Jews suffered in the siege,
Josephus narrates many things, which a small book like this cannot contain.
Titus his son, two years.
The senate proclaimed him a god.
And when he accepted being proclaimed as such,
he died suddenly.
[Domitian] his brother, sixteen years.
This man drove out the Chaldeans and philosophers from Rome.
And he commanded that no vine be planted within the city.
And he forbade anyone from castrating a male.
And Cornelia, a virgin priestess, was accused of corruption,
and was buried alive.
And while the preaching of Christ was growing powerfully,
Patrophilus the philosopher said to his master Ursinus:
"What is this,
that Theodora, head of the wise men of Athens,
and Africanus the Alexandrian philosopher,
and Martinus of Badu (Bardu? {OCR?}),
and many others,
worship a crucified man,
while they do not occupy themselves with wealth,
and are powerful in word and deed?" And he answered:
"Even the gods and their priests become his disciples.
For since his disciples do not give their souls over to hateful customs of sin,
this testifies that their teaching is truly better than all teachings."
And when Domitian heard these things, he was amazed,
and he stopped the persecution.
At this time Apollonius of Tyana {OCR?} displayed talismans,
and did everything by demons.
And he used to say:
"Woe is me!
Woe is me!
For the Son of Mary preceded me by ... {OCR?} one year."
Afterwards he fell into sickness,
and his body wasted away,
and he died in the garden of Sallust.
[Trajan], nineteen years {OCR?}.
This man stirred up a persecution against the Christians,
in which Simeon son of Cleopas of Jerusalem,
and John the Apostle,
and Ignatius of Antioch were crowned.
And Pliny the Second, the governor, killed many Christians.
